home.about.headline: What this place is for
home.about.text1: de-press is a non-profit space for empathy and emotional support.
home.about.text2: There are no likes, ratings or public reactions here. A story can simply be heard, quietly and without being turned into a measure of its worth.
home.about.text3: The project is built around a simple idea: asking for help is human, and sometimes being heard is already a form of support.
about.hiddenTitle: A quiet harbour for difficult moments
about.mission: de-press is a space for emotional support built on the principles of privacy and consent. It is a place where you can say what is hard to say elsewhere, without having to perform for an audience or play a familiar social role.
about.meaningText: A story doesn't need a score. A person doesn't need an audience. Sometimes it's enough to simply speak up anonymously, write what you feel, and be heard. Nobody forces conversation on you — it is always your choice.
about.tired: Sometimes the problem lives in the familiar language of social media: likes, reposts, public reactions, other people's approval, and the effort to play a role instead of being yourself.
about.goodNews: So this place is deliberately quieter: fewer notifications and signals, less noise, but more room to simply be heard.
about.products.authorChat: - Only the author starts a chat
about.products.emotionMaps: - Emotion maps stay on your device
about.products.helper: - A Helper is not a therapist by default
about.tableIntro: This project grew out of a personal need for a safe space.
about.goal: We will build a quiet, calm place where anyone can be heard and understood.
about.howText1: You come with your story and choose for yourself whom to talk to and when. You don't have to answer when things are hard, but you can be heard.
about.howText2: If you want, you can simply write how you feel and be heard without judgment.
about.howText3: What you share, how much you share and whether you want a conversation are your decisions.
values.intro: de-press is a non-profit platform for quiet emotional support. We believe everyone deserves to be heard and understood.
values.notRules: They are not rules for the sake of rules. They are the boundaries that keep this place quiet.
values.next: Here is what that means in practice.
values.p1.text: A difficult experience is not a competition. Public likes and ratings are not hidden here — they don't exist in the data model at all.
values.p2.text: Someone else's story is not an invitation to a heated debate. Sometimes quiet participation is enough — shown in reactions only the author can see.
values.p3.text: A dialogue doesn't exist until its author opens it. Voice notes are deleted when the conversation closes — only an explicit choice keeps them.
values.p4.text: AI, when used, is clearly identified. It does not diagnose, impersonate a human or replace human support.
values.p5.text: Self-help practices live right in your browser, in IndexedDB, and are never sent to the server. The server knows nothing about them.
values.p6.text: There is no analytics, no metrics, no ads and no fingerprinting in the code. The project doesn't need to hold your attention, so there is nothing about you for it to measure.
values.p7.text: This is not an emergency service. In a crisis, the right next step is real-world emergency help, not an app.
values.p8.text: A Helper is there to listen, not to pose as a doctor. Therapy here comes only from living people: payment goes directly, wallet to wallet, and the platform is not a middleman.
values.p9.text2: Anyone can read the code and, if they wish, run their own copy of the platform. We don't keep personal data without the user knowing.
values.hear.text: Not every story needs an answer. Sometimes it's enough to simply speak up, put your feelings into words and be heard without judgment.
values.hearReady: There is always room for people who know how to listen

safety.nowTitle: If things are really bad right now
safety.nowText: de-press.co is a quiet harbour, but it is not emergency help. If you are in danger or having thoughts of harming yourself — seek help right now. You don't have to cope alone.
safety.callText: 112 is the universal emergency number, 103 is an ambulance (in some countries). Both work from any phone, including one with no credit.
safety.stepsTitle: What you can do right now
safety.step1: Tell a live person nearby — even just “I feel awful”. You don't have to explain everything: one sentence is enough to not be left alone.
safety.step2: Call 112 or 103 and say that you need help.
safety.step3: Don't stay alone: ask someone to stay with you until help arrives.
safety.step4: If you can — move away from anything you could hurt yourself with, and stay away from dangerous places.
safety.step5: Breathe slowly: in for four counts, out for six. It doesn't solve everything, but it helps you survive the acute wave.
safety.notHereText: de-press.co has no likes, ratings or public comments. Your story will be heard, not judged. Only you can start a chat. The AI assistant is always labelled, makes no diagnoses and never replaces people.
safety.longTermTitle: If it has been hard for a long time
safety.longTermText: de-press.co is not medicine and not a replacement for therapy. If the state lasts for weeks or interferes with living — see a doctor or a psychotherapist. Asking for help is normal.

meta.privacy.description: What de-press.co stores and what it doesn't: anonymity as a property of the system, no trackers, no IP logs, no behavioral analytics.
privacy.stored.telegramId: Telegram id — only when signing in via the Telegram Mini App.
privacy.lead: People may bring things here they do not feel able to tell elsewhere. So the project is direct about data: what is stored, what is not, and where the boundaries are.
privacy.stored.session: An anonymous session — a UUID in a cookie. To the server, that's you: no registration, no name.
privacy.stored.alias: A pseudonym — whatever you type, or nothing at all. Separately, we keep internal help flags — a record of who has been helped; tying them to an account is optional.
privacy.stored.email: An email — only if you created an account or asked for notifications. Otherwise the field just stays empty.
privacy.stored.stories: Stories, dialogues, messages — that is the project itself. Their author, for us, is that same UUID, never a person with a name.
privacy.stored.voice: Voice messages and video circles — files inside a dialogue. We keep them only with the author's consent.
privacy.stored.notifications: Notifications, reports, blocks — private events of the person who receives them, pseudonymous like everything else.
privacy.stored.solana: A Solana address for thanking a helper is published by the helper — if they want to.
privacy.notHere.ip: IP addresses. The code never writes them down. The only place an IP plays any role is the rate limit protecting the translation catalog: for an hour, the cache holds a hash salted with a secret key. The address itself isn't kept even there.
privacy.notHere.userAgent: A User-Agent — never read, never written.
privacy.notHere.logs: Access logs with IPs and User-Agents: in production, nginx writes a privacy-first format.
privacy.notHere.analytics: Google Analytics, Yandex.Metrica, Sentry profiles — no behavioral analytics.
privacy.notHere.likes: Likes and views — they don't exist in the data model: quiet empathy instead of a reach race.
privacy.notHere.keys: Private keys and payments. Money travels wallet → wallet, and the platform only sees the status.
privacy.retentionTitle: How long any of it lives
privacy.retention.voice: Voice messages disappear along with the dialogue. They stay only if the author chose to keep them.
privacy.retention.video: Video circles are deleted when a dialogue closes.
privacy.retention.session: The anonymous session lives in your cookie — and behind it there is nothing but a UUID and the optional fields from the list above.
privacy.verifyTitle: You should not have to take our word for it
privacy.verify.registration: No feature requires registration. Email and Telegram are optional notification channels, not a way in.
privacy.verify.data: The data holds no real names, phone numbers, birth dates, locations, avatars or social graphs.
privacy.verify.code: The code holds no pixels, no ads, no browser fingerprinting.
privacy.verify.practices: Self-help practices run right in your browser and never leave your device.
privacy.verify.selfHosted: Every line above is a property of the code, not a promise. The platform is self-hostable: run your own instance and look into the database tables yourself.

support.title: Support
support.lead: de-press is a quiet place for people who are struggling right now. There are no ads or subscriptions here, and no one monetizes other people's pain. The project is kept going by volunteers and by people who care.
support.manifest.noFee: There are no paid features and no hidden fees. Everything you send goes directly to supporting the project.
support.manifest.noSubscription: There is nothing to pay for by subscription, and every user is equal in what they can do and in their rights.
support.manifest.noMonetize: Difficult experiences are not a business model. There are no sales metrics built around people’s pain.
